title: Room temperature sensor fault
shortDescription: The indoor room temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
GE air conditioners display E1 when the room thermistor reading is outside the expected range. The control board cannot regulate cooling without a valid temperature signal and shuts down the compressor.

The fault is usually caused by a disconnected sensor harness or a failed thermistor. Replacing the sensor restores normal operation.
symptoms: Fan may run but no cooling

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the unit for 5 minutes and reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Open the front grille and reseat the thermistor connector on the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Test resistance against spec; replace if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the control board is suspected.
videoSearchQuery: GE air conditioner E1 error fix

faq.q: Can I keep using the AC with E1?
faq.a: No, the compressor is locked out until the sensor reads correctly.

title: Evaporator coil sensor fault
shortDescription: The indoor coil thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the evaporator (indoor) coil temperature sensor is reporting an invalid value. The control uses this sensor for freeze protection and defrost; without it, cooling is disabled.

Check the sensor harness first, then test resistance. A failed thermistor is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor mount
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the thermistor clip is secure on the evaporator coil.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and compare to spec at room temperature.

whenToCallPro: If sensor tests good but error persists, board replacement is needed.

faq.a: Only temporarily if the sensor is bad.

title: Indoor fan motor fault
shortDescription: The indoor blower motor is not reaching commanded speed.
fullDescription:
GE window units flag E3 when the blower motor tach signal is missing or the motor is stalled. Without airflow over the evaporator, the unit cannot cool safely and shuts down.

Common causes include a seized bearing, blocked blower wheel, or a failed motor capacitor.
symptoms: Fan does not spin or hums

fixSteps.title: Unplug and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the front cover and check the blower wheel for obstructions.

fixSteps.title: Spin by hand
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate the blower wheel to verify free movement.

whenToCallPro: If the motor itself needs replacement on a sealed system.
videoSearchQuery: GE window AC E3 fan motor

faq.a: It is a safety lockout; the unit prevents coil icing.

title: EEPROM data error
shortDescription: The control board memory chip is unreadable.
fullDescription:
E4 means the microcontroller cannot read its calibration EEPROM. This is almost always a control board failure or a firmware corruption event after a power surge.

A full power cycle sometimes clears the fault; otherwise the main control board must be replaced.
symptoms: Unit will not respond to buttons

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes, then plug in.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: Order the matching board for your model and swap.

whenToCallPro: Most homeowners should call a pro for control board work.

faq.a: No, GE window AC firmware is not user-updatable.

title: Communication error
shortDescription: The display board cannot communicate with the main board.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates loss of the serial link between the user interface and main control. Loose ribbon cables and moisture intrusion are typical culprits.

Reseat connectors first; if the fault persists, replace the user interface board.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Open front bezel and firmly reseat ribbon cables.

whenToCallPro: If reseating fails and a replacement UI board is unavailable.

faq.a: Yes, condensation on the UI board can cause E5.

title: Compressor protection
shortDescription: The compressor overload or thermal protector tripped.
fullDescription:
E6 is shown when the compressor fails to start or trips its overload. Causes include low line voltage, a failed run capacitor, or a seized compressor.

Most diagnostic steps require a technician familiar with sealed system service.

fixSteps.title: Verify outlet voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 115V at the receptacle under load.

fixSteps.title: Test capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge and measure microfarads against spec.

whenToCallPro: If the compressor itself is suspect, call a pro.

faq.a: Yes, brownouts under 105V often trigger this fault.

title: Outdoor coil sensor fault
shortDescription: The condenser coil temperature sensor is invalid.
fullDescription:
E7 indicates the outdoor coil thermistor is open, shorted, or disconnected. This sensor is used for high-side overload protection.

Reseat the connector at the main board and verify resistance with a meter.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for chafing or pinched wires near the chassis.

whenToCallPro: If the sensor is sealed inside the condenser jacket.

faq.q: Why does E7 only appear when hot?
faq.a: The fault is masked at low temps; high temps push the sensor outside spec.

title: Air sensor failure
shortDescription: The intake air sensor reading is out of range.
fullDescription:
AS is shown by some GE smart window units when the intake air thermistor is open or shorted. It is functionally similar to E1 but on newer Wi-Fi models.

Replace the sensor or the wire harness assembly.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Order the GE-spec sensor and swap on the harness.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed unless harness is damaged.

faq.a: Wi-Fi remains online but cooling is disabled.

title: Coil sensor failure
shortDescription: Evaporator coil sensor fault on smart models.
fullDescription:
CS appears on GE Wi-Fi window units when the evaporator coil thermistor is invalid. The fault disables compressor operation.

The sensor is mounted to the coil with a spring clip and is field replaceable.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Pull old clip and install new sensor in same position.

whenToCallPro: If the coil is damaged during sensor removal.

faq.a: Yes, fan mode is unaffected by CS.

title: Drain pan full
fullDescription:
FL signals that the condensate pan is full or the float switch is stuck. Portable and some window units use a float to prevent overflow.

Drain the unit per the owner manual; if FL persists, the float switch needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Drain unit
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the drain plug and empty the pan into a container.

whenToCallPro: If the float switch is integrated with the pump.
videoSearchQuery: GE portable AC FL error drain

faq.a: Most portable units self-evaporate, but humid days may require manual draining.

title: GE E8 — Compressor Drive Fault
shortDescription: GE Air Conditioner error E8: The compressor inverter or drive circuit has reported an error and stopped the compressor.
fullDescription: Error code E8 on GE air conditioners indicates the compressor inverter or drive circuit has reported an error and stopped the compressor. This condition normally locks out cooling or heating until the fault is cleared. Common causes include a defective inverter/compressor module, a loose or damaged wiring harness between the component and the main control board, or a failure of the control board itself. Begin with a hard power reset, then inspect the inverter/compressor module and its wiring before considering board replacement.
symptoms: E8 shown on the indoor display or remote
Compressor or fan does not start

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the unit from power for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the error returns.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Open the service panel and verify all connectors at the main control board are fully seated and undamaged.

fixSteps.title: Test the suspect component
fixSteps.instruction: Use a multimeter to verify resistance or continuity of the affected sensor or component, and compare against service manual specs.

fixSteps.title: Replace the failed part
fixSteps.instruction: Order the matching replacement part for your model, install it in the same orientation, and reconnect all wiring before re-testing.

whenToCallPro: If basic checks do not clear the E8 code, an HVAC technician should be called to verify refrigerant pressures and inverter operation.
videoSearchQuery: GE air conditioner E8 error fix
